title: OCIA Session I: The Journey of Faith
reading: OCIA Session I Overview & Scripture: Acts 17:24–28, Psalm 42:1–2, Hebrews 11:1–6, Jeremiah 29:11–13. Catechism: CCC 27–30, CCC 31–38, CCC 142–156.

content.overview: The Order of Christian Initiation of Adults is not a mere academic course, but a gradual spiritual journey into full communion with the Catholic Church. It is structured in four distinct stages: Inquiry (asking questions), Catechumenate (deeper study and formation), Purification & Enlightenment (intense spiritual reflection during Lent), and Mystagogy (deepening understanding of the sacraments after Easter).
keyPoints: The Universal Search: Every human being is born with a 'God-shaped vacuum' in their heart. As St. Augustine famously wrote: 'You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.'

God’s Response (Divine Revelation): God stepped into history through Covenants (Abraham, Moses) and spoke fully by becoming man in Jesus Christ, reaching us today through Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition.

What is Faith: Faith is our personal response to God’s invitation—a supernatural gift combining Trust, Truth, and the harmonious balance of Faith and Reason ('two wings on which the human spirit rises').

questions: Where in your life have you felt the 'restlessness' that St. Augustine talks about?
Looking back at your life's path, how do you see God gently drawing you toward this moment?

title: OCIA Session II: The Trinity
requirements: Explore the mystery of the Holy Trinity, the distinction between nature and person, Scripture and Tradition, and the early Church ecumenical councils.

title: Scripture and Tradition (Divine Revelation)
questions: How do Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition work together to hand on God's revelation?
What practices can you adopt to read and engage with the Bible more regularly?

title: Old Testament & New Testament
reading: Explore the overarching narrative structure of the Old and New Testaments.
questions: How does the Old Testament prepare the way for the coming of Jesus Christ in the New Testament?
Which part of Scripture has surprised or inspired you the most so far?

title: Story of Salvation
reading: Study the divine timeline: Creation, Fall, and Redemption.
questions: How do you see the story of salvation history playing out in human history and in your own life?
What does God's persistent pursuit of humanity despite the Fall tell you about His character?

title: Following Jesus/Who is He?
questions: Who is Jesus Christ to you personally, and what does it mean to truly follow Him?
What is one area of your life where you feel called to surrender more fully to Christ's leadership?

title: Communion of Saints and Angels
reading: Reflect on the spiritual reality of the heavenly hosts and the communion of believers.
questions: How does the concept of the Communion of Saints alter your perspective on death and spiritual community?
Do you have a favorite saint you look to for intercession or inspiration? Why?

title: Incarnation
reading: Study the mystery of God taking on human flesh.
questions: Why is the Incarnation—God becoming man—such a central and revolutionary truth of Christianity?
How does God entering human history change how you view everyday human life and physical creation?

title: Paschal Mystery: Jesus’ Death & Resurrection
reading: Study the ultimate saving act of Christ's Passion, Death, and Resurrection.
questions: How do Jesus' suffering and resurrection give meaning to the trials and difficulties in your own life?
What does new life in Christ look like practically for someone walking this OCIA journey?

title: What is the Church / Why Do I Need the Church?
questions: Why is belonging to the visible Church community necessary rather than just practicing faith privately?
What does it mean to you that the Church is both a human institution and a divine mystery?

title: Church History
reading: Survey major milestones in the 2,000-year history of the Catholic Church.
questions: What stands out to you most about how the Church has survived and grown through history despite human flaws?
How does knowing the historical roots of the Church strengthen your confidence in its teachings?

title: Prayer and the Liturgical Year / Advent
questions: How has your prayer life evolved during your time exploring the OCIA process?
How can entering into the rhythms of the Liturgical Year (like Advent) deepen your spiritual focus?

title: Role of Mary in the Church
questions: How has your understanding of Mary's role as Mother of God and Mother of the Church developed?
In what ways can Mary's example of radical 'Fiat' (yes) to God inspire your own spiritual walk?

title: Introduction to the Sacraments
questions: What is a sacrament, and why are visible, tangible signs necessary for conveying invisible grace?
Which sacrament are you most looking forward to receiving, and why?

title: Baptism & Confirmation
questions: What does it mean to be cleansed, adopted, and sealed with the Holy Spirit through Baptism and Confirmation?
How does the Sacrament of Confirmation empower you to live out your faith publicly?

title: The Holy Eucharist & Walk Through the Mass
reading: Study the source and summit of Christian life alongside the structure of the Mass.
questions: How does your perspective on the Eucharist shift when considering the Real Presence of Christ?
Which part of the Mass (Liturgy of the Word or Liturgy of the Eucharist) do you find most engaging?

title: Reconciliation & Anointing of the Sick
questions: How does the Sacrament of Reconciliation offer psychological peace alongside spiritual healing?
Why is God's mercy viewed as a gift rather than something to fear?

title: Marriage & Holy Orders
questions: How do the Sacraments at the Service of Communion (Matrimony and Holy Orders) build up the body of Christ?
What does it mean to view marriage as a path to holiness and mutual sanctification?

title: What is Lent? Prayer, Fasting, and Almsgiving
reading: Explore the Lenten pillars: Prayer (Devotions, Rosary, Lectio Divina), Fasting, and Almsgiving.
questions: How do the three pillars of Lent (prayer, fasting, almsgiving) help reorient our hearts toward God?
What practical Lenten discipline do you find most challenging, and how do you plan to approach it?

title: Catholic Moral Vision
reading: Study the foundations of Christian morality, grace, virtues, and true human happiness.
questions: How does Catholic morality differ from a mere list of rules, focusing instead on relationship and virtue?
Which virtue do you feel you most need God's grace to cultivate in your daily life?

title: Meaning of Holy Week / How-to's of Reconciliation
reading: Compendium #111-131: Deep dive into the Triduum and preparing for Confession.
questions: Why is walking closely through the events of Holy Week so vital for a Christian's spiritual growth?
What steps can you take to prepare your heart and mind to make a good Confession?

title: Human Sexuality
questions: How does the Church's teaching on human sexuality protect and honor the dignity of the human person?
In a culture with differing views, how can we better understand sexuality as a gift ordered toward love and life?

title: The Last Things: Heaven, Hell, Purgatory
questions: How does keeping eternity in mind (Heaven, Hell, Purgatory) change how you live out your everyday choices?
What gives you hope when you reflect on the final destination of the human soul?

title: Dignity of Life
questions: What does the consistent ethic of life teach us about the sacredness of human life from conception to natural death?
How can a community better support and protect vulnerable human life in daily practice?

title: Social Justice
questions: How are works of charity and works of justice intertwined in Catholic social teaching?
Which principle of Catholic social teaching resonates most deeply with your personal values?

title: Conversion: An On-Going Process
questions: Why is conversion not a one-time event, but an ongoing daily journey of turning toward God?
What signs of spiritual growth have you noticed in yourself since starting this class?

title: Discernment & Decision Making
questions: How do prayer, Scripture, and wise counsel play a role in Christian discernment?
What steps do you take when trying to discern God's will for a major life decision?

title: Evangelization
questions: What does it mean to share the 'Good News' of Christ through your everyday actions and words?
What hesitations do you sometimes feel about sharing your faith, and how can you overcome them?

title: The Holy Spirit & Life of Grace
reading: Reflect on Pentecost and living a life energized by the Holy Spirit.
questions: How have you experienced the guidance or comfort of the Holy Spirit in your life recently?
What does living a 'life of grace' look like in practice day-to-day?

title: Role of the Laity
reading: Compendium #189-191: Understanding the mission of lay Catholics in the world.
questions: How are lay Catholics uniquely positioned to bring Christian values into secular workplaces and families?
In what ways do you feel called to serve within your parish community?

title: What’s Next: Living as a Catholic
reading: Transitioning from the OCIA candidate phase into active, lifelong parish life.
questions: How do you plan to continue your spiritual education and community involvement after OCIA concludes?
What is your biggest hope for your continued walk as an active member of the Catholic Church?
